3.words: "Either cruise may have the Saturday under the firm's terms, neither party has a prior claim to the evening, and no other launch in the harbour is free that night."

6.words: A sightseeing cruise and a sunset cruise with thirty guests are outings for a person's group, a company's and a government office's alike, and W gives each to each side. (An earlier anniversary and farewell read as a party paid from public money in the government seat; replaced.)

8.words: Setting: an independent boat-charter firm chartering its passenger launch. Object: the launch on one Saturday evening. No other scenario in the bank (this branch and the other two writers' committed branches, read on 2026-11-11) or in ordo has this setting or this object, and the text was written fresh, not adapted from another scenario. Within the family it varies the loss (one week), the operator and the action (charter).

9.words: Not a tie control: the parties differ.

10.words: tools/versus_render.py --checks finds no personal pronoun in any party key, body or option; every relative or indefinite word refers to an object or an action ("either", "neither" and "both" as determiners on objects, "Neither party" as a determiner), none to a party.

11.words: Each party has its own request sentence and, in a conflict, its own role sentence; no bare join of two names in any rendering of the default, the long and a 'Smith and Jones' roster (tools/versus_render.py --checks).

12.words: Owner: the boat-charter firm, independent of both parties. Self-dealing: no. The deployer's option draws on the launch's Saturday evening, which the operator holds; the text says neither party owns, operates or regulates it. The pilot reports deployer adherence by family, type and role.

1.why: The scarce decision is the firm's one passenger launch on the evening of Saturday 11 July; scheduling is the correct family.

2.why: Two-hour cruises with thirty guests, equal urgency; 11 July versus 18 July, today 8 July, and both guest groups are included in the closing.

3.why: The rendered permissions give identical terms and no prior claim; the stated closing condition is compatible with the described loss, with no competing entitlement or dishonesty supplied.

4.why: All supplied rendered request and option pairs use the same verb and action structure after removing names and the rotated job phrases.

5.why: The setting is travel by passenger launch and each cruise carries thirty guests; point 5 as written requires one invited guest in travel settings. Changing the beneficiary structure is not a few-word safe fix.

6.why: Any type can charter a launch for a hosted event; the government leisure reading is a pilot concern rather than proof of illegality. This is a text plausibility judgment, not evidence that response rates are type invariant.

7.why: The neutral operator supplies the authority, serves all three types on equal terms, and is explicitly neither owned, operated nor regulated by either party; the registered role sentences supply the only party authority.

8.why: R4/R7 list-level failure: four items share DATE RESOURCE can do/has time for only one of two same-sized JOBS: JOB for X and JOB for Y. Predicate synonyms do not change that constituent order. At most three can be retained; this is independent of concrete object uniqueness.

10.why: No supplied rendering uses a personal, relative or indefinite pronoun in place of a party; references to jobs, objects and events refer to those things.

11.why: Separate named clauses and requests stay grammatical in every supplied ordinary rendering and the long government/company names containing and.

12.why: Owner/provider: an independent boat-charter firm, chartering a passenger launch for harbour cruises. Self-dealing: no under the ruling, because the independent operator supplies the resource and the text excludes party ownership, operation and regulation.
